title: Annual gutter clearance and maintenance schedule
subtitle: Clearing debris, checking falls, and rodding downpipes before the autumn rains
excerpt: A blocked gutter overflows behind the fascia, wetting the wall and eventually the ceiling below. A sagging gutter on the wrong fall pools water that feeds moss and leaks joints. Annual clearance in late autumn takes 2 to 4 hours and prevents damp wall repairs costing many times more.
sourceNotes: BRE (Building Research Establishment) guidance on wall dampness from gutter and downpipe defects (Good Repair Guides, public domain). NHBC guidance on guttering and rainwater goods. BS EN 12056-3 for gutter fall recommendations.

glossaryTerms.definition: The slope of a gutter from the highest point to the outlet. Typically 1:600 (1 mm drop per 600 mm of run) for standard 112 mm half-round guttering.

content.text: Gutters do one job: take rainwater from the roof edge to a downpipe before it runs down the wall. Leaf debris, moss, and bird nests block them within one to three years in most UK gardens. A blocked gutter in a heavy shower overflows directly behind the fascia board, wetting the top of the wall just where it is most vulnerable.

attrs.title: Working at height
attrs.body: Ladder set at 75°: 1 out for every 4 up. Three-point contact at all times. Do not overreach; come down and move the ladder. A scaffold tower or extending gutter vacuum is safer than a ladder for a full house run.

content.text: Late autumn (October or November): most leaves have fallen but the heaviest rains are still to come. Clearing now ensures the gutters run free through winter.
After any storm that brings large volumes of leaf fall or debris from nearby trees.
Spring inspection: check for winter damage, broken joints, and new moss growth.
Start at the end away from the downpipe and work toward it. Scoop debris by hand or with a gutter scoop into a bucket hanging from the ladder. Do not push debris toward the downpipe.
Run a hose from the far end after clearing. Watch for water pooling at any point: this indicates a section has sagged out of its correct
Check all joint connectors and gutter brackets. A joint that is dry and cracked will leak; replace the rubber seal or the whole connector.
Rod the downpipe with a drain rod or a flexible brush. Insert from the top, push to the base, withdraw slowly to avoid forcing blockages into the drain at the bottom.
Run the hose again and watch the outlet at ground level. Flow should be steady and immediate. If it is slow or backs up, the underground drain connection is blocked.

A standard 112 mm half-round gutter should fall at 1:600 (1.7 mm per metre). To check: hold a spirit level along the top edge of the gutter and measure how far below horizontal the outlet end sits over a measured run. Adjust the bracket height at the high end by loosening the fascia screw, re-setting, and re-screwing. Re-check with the hose.

Mesh guards over the gutter opening reduce the frequency of clearance needed but do not eliminate it. Fine mesh can accumulate composted silt that still needs flushing. Pine needles pass through most mesh guards. Inspect annually even with guards fitted.

rows.symptom: Gutter fills and overflows even when clear of debris
rows.cause: Gutter is undersized for the roof catchment area, or the outlet is too small
rows.fix: A standard 112 mm half-round gutter handles approximately 50 m² of roof area. If the roof is larger, add a second downpipe or upgrade to 150 mm guttering.

rows.symptom: Water comes down inside the wall after gutter clearance
rows.cause: Gutter is correctly draining but water has entered a gap at the back of the gutter, behind the fascia
rows.fix: Check the gutter front edge is level or slightly higher than the back. Water should not be able to flow backward over the rear edge onto the fascia.
